A truce has cooled the trade conflict, but neither country has done anything to limit the outbreak of new hostilities

Donald Trump’s trade wars have largely fallen off the headlines. Fears of new tariffs flare up from time to time when the US president goes off the rails – for instance, threatening to end US trade with countries with which it has a deficit unless the Federal Reserve cuts interest rates. But the sense that the world’s two largest economies are plowing ahead into an overt economic conflagration has taken a back seat to other, more salient fears, about Trump ending American democracy, AI killing us all and stuff like that.

The sense of calm is misleading. Under the radar, the world is marching toward an economic war of potentially epic proportions, one that, history suggests, could well spill over into the real thing.

Eisenkot says Netanyahu trying to ‘delegitimise’ results

Israeli opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot accused Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu of leading a “campaign of delegitimisation” against Israel’s inconclusive election results, after Central Elections Committee said the vote was valid.

“The despicable and malicious attempt to deny the election results, undermine the will of the public, smear an entire community, and drag Israel into another round of elections has failed,” Eisenkot wrote in Hebrew on X.

item.title: [www.middleeasteye.net] Israel intentionally released footage of Mossad operatives in Iran to provoke mass arrests, ex-chief says
item.description:
Israel intentionally released footage of Mossad operatives in Iran to provoke mass arrests, ex-chief says

Former Mossad chief David Barnea has said Israel intentionally released images of their covert operation in Iran during the June 2025 conflict to provoke mass arrests and make it harder for Iranian forces to find real Israeli agents.

“One of the reasons we immediately released an official video on the morning of Operation Rising Lion, with the Mossad logo, was to protect the agents who were there,” Barnea said, according to comments The Jerusalem Post reported on 25 October.

Barnea said the leak of the footage of Israeli operations in Iran was not just an attempt to showcase the Mossad’s reach but also a strategy to overwhelm Iranian counterintelligence, causing them to make mass arrests, making it more difficult to distinguish operatives from ordinary citizens.

“We wanted to make sure they arrested so many people in Iran that they wouldn’t be able to distinguish the wheat from the chaff and would eventually release everyone,” he said.

Barnea said Iranian authorities arrested 21,000 people during the operation.

item.title: [www.middleeasteye.net] Aipac is now a toxic brand. The Michigan Senate race is only one example
item.description:
Aipac is now a toxic brand. The Michigan Senate race is only one example

Submitted by Mitchell Plitnick on Wed, 10/28/2026 - 15:28
The pro-Israel lobbying group has worked tirelessly to portray an apartheid regime that is committing genocide as a warm and friendly country - US voters have finally wised up
Michigan Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed speaks to supporters on 1 November 2026 in Michigan (AFP)
Off

“A lobby is like a night flower: it thrives in the dark and dies in the sun.” So said Steve Rosen, former foreign policy director of the American Israel Public Affairs Committee (Aipac) in a memo to a fellow staffer. Rosen would later be fired amid a major scandal involving espionage in passing classified US information to Israel. 

Rosen was correct about the danger to a lobbying organisation that publicity poses. But in December 2021, Aipac decided to test that theory by creating two political action committees (Pacs) that enabled it to take part directly in political campaigns.

The results were mixed, and Aipac recently announced that it was closing one of the Pacs it had set up. 

Aipac had been an advocacy organisation, promoting Israel’s interests, but it did not fund campaigns directly, nor did it endorse or fund political candidates. 

In many ways, that made it more effective. It could do things like issue a congressional report card which rated every member of Congress’s support of Israel. Then other groups that were actual Pacs could use those reports to decide which candidates they should be contributing to. 

Aipac’s non-profit status allows it to lobby Congress on behalf of Israel while claiming it acts strictly in support of the wishes of pro-Israel Americans. It thus avoids having to register as an agent of a foreign government. 

Meanwhile, Aipac’s sister organisation, the American Israel Education Fund, which is registered as an education non-profit, refrains from direct lobbying but offers vacation tours to Israel for members of Congress, under the rubric of “education”.

This strategy was effective for decades. Aipac’s bipartisan reach was strong, and it was often remarked by a credulous media how Israel was, somehow, the one subject Democrats and Republicans could come together on.

Changing opinion

That began to change in recent years. 

The reasons are complicated, but the result was that presidential and congressional candidates, mostly among Democrats, were suddenly accepting the idea that annual military aid to Israel, which had risen to $3.8bn annually, should be conditioned on Israel conforming to the requirements of United States law and adhering with United States policy.

It’s a mark of how successful Aipac had been that such obvious conditions, which were already mandated by US law, were considered controversial. 

But a growing awareness of the conditions that Palestinians were living under in the West Bank and Gaza Strip was changing the minds of many of Israel’s liberal supporters. 

Aipac decided to take the step of getting more directly involved in political campaigns to try to stifle the number of advocates for Palestine in Congress while the number of them was still very small.

They created two Pacs: Aipac-Pac could contribute directly to candidates’ campaigns; and the United for Democracy Project (UDP), a super Pac, which cannot directly fund campaigns, but can spend an unlimited amount on advertising and other public advocacy to support their chosen candidates.

Aipac has long been known for its lobbying, but now, its support for individual candidates could be tracked in a measurable way, making it the perfect symbol of money in politics.

Aipac was attacked for its influence in Washington and was more easily assailed than other lobbying groups because it advocated for the interests of a foreign country. 

AIPAC spent millions to unseat me. Here’s why they’re now losing: Ex-congressman | Jamaal Bowman
Read More »

Aipac’s argument that it was an American group representing the interests of America’s pro-Israel community has worked for decades to protect the organisation from the limitations it would face as a registered agent of a foreign government.

But in the court of public opinion, that technical argument holds little weight. People understand that Aipac defends and promotes the interests of a foreign country. 

Now that it was openly spending on campaigns and giving money to candidates, it could be caught up in the general distaste the American public has for the role of big money in politics.

And the Aipac name started becoming toxic. Much of this was led by Bernie Sanders, who was among the first to recognise how vulnerable Aipac was to this sort of public shaming. 

Instead of impacting American politics with its newfound ability to spend great amounts of money, Aipac only further tarnished Israel’s once popular image in the United States.

This was especially true for Democrats, whom Israel, under Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, had been alienating for years, even though most American Jews are Democrats.

Battleground state

The decline of Israel’s image and the toxicity of Aipac were most clearly on display in the election campaigns this year in the battleground state of Michigan.

In the upcoming election, Democrats have long been expected to win back the House of Representatives and now have a good chance of winning the Senate too. One of the key states in the election is Michigan.

The Republican candidate in Michigan, Mike Rogers, is a known quantity, a staunchly right-wing man whose candidacy is backed by big corporations, extremist Christian groups, and Donald Trump.

Mike Rogers’ campaign quietly asked Aipac to refrain from supporting Rogers. That is a mark of how toxic Aipac has become

Abdul El-Sayed became the Democratic nominee after overcoming huge obstacles related to his views on Israel and Palestine, the war on Iran, and, most of all, the simple fact of his being a Muslim.

He won a bruising primary against Congresswoman Haley Stevens, who had been an Aipac candidate for years.

Stevens defeated Andy Levin in 2022, with a great deal of help from Aipac. Levin, who comes from a Michigan political dynasty and is a prominent leader in his Jewish community, was a self-identified Zionist, but a liberal one who believed in a two-state solution. 

But that was nothing compared to Aipac’s support for Stevens against El-Sayed.

In total, Stevens outspent El-Sayed in the campaign by a 12-to-one margin. Aipac and other pro-Israel groups spent more than $30m between their own advertising and donations to Stevens’ campaign. 

Stevens kept a distance from some of the often vicious anti-Muslim rhetoric aimed at El-Sayed by her supporters, including Aipac. But she was not forceful in denouncing it, and this was noted and would only grow worse when El-Sayed faced a Republican.

El-Sayed eventually defeated Stevens in a closely contested primary. Even as she denied that her association with Aipac might have hurt her chances of winning, Stevens inadvertently hinted that it did.

“I think that there [were] a lot of people talking about it, and they didn’t love it because maybe they don’t understand what the group is. Aipac is a group of six million Jewish Americans… a lot of people are deeply frustrated that [Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin] Netanyahu has failed to give us peace,” she said.

Over the weekend, a dramatic turn of events took place when the Michigan Democratic Party kicked Stevens out of its ranks, after she endorsed Michigan’s GOP Senate nominee, Mike Rogers - over Democrat Abdul El-Sayed.

"Congresswoman Stevens is not a current member of the Michigan Democratic Party, nor will she be in the future," the state party’s chair, Curtis Hertel, said in a post Sunday on X.

Islamaphobic rhetoric

Meanwhile, El-Sayed’s Republican opponent turned up the Islamophobic rhetoric, consistently and falsely accusing El-Sayed of working with the Muslim Brotherhood, and of saying that the United States “deserved” the attacks of 11 September 2001. 

Yet despite that level of mudslinging, Rogers’ campaign, soon after the primaries ended, quietly asked Aipac to refrain from supporting Rogers. That is a mark of how toxic Aipac has become. 

From Michigan to Missouri: Democratic primaries deliver mixed bag on Israel and Gaza
Read More »

Eventually, Rogers, whose base of support includes some of the most zealous and extreme supporters of Israel from the evangelical Christian community, publicly welcomed and received support from Aipac. 

But his reluctance to initially accept Aipac money despite his very proud right-wing views shows how ubiquitous hostility toward Aipac is.

The saga of Abdul El-Sayed and the Michigan Senate race is only one example of the toxicity of Aipac’s brand. The widespread distaste for the group explains why it is pulling itself out of the game of direct financing of candidates.

Aipac will maintain the UDP super Pac, in the hope that it can continue to influence races quietly, with few people noticing that it is Aipac behind attack ads which often have nothing to do with Israel but serve to denigrate candidates who might have the slightest tendency toward advocacy for the rights of Palestinians. 

But if UDP can also be dragged into the light, it - like Aipac-Pac - will also wither and die. Aipac works tirelessly to portray an apartheid regime that is committing genocide as a warm, friendly country. Like a lobby, that effort cannot withstand the sunlight, and even Aipac’s own officials know it.

item.title: [www.middleeasteye.net] Iran's foreign ministry says exchanges with US ongoing via mediators: AFP
item.description:
Iran's foreign ministry says exchanges with US ongoing via mediators: AFP

Iran said that negotiations with the US were ongoing via mediators, according to AFP, despite withdrawing from talks on Sunday.

A draft proposal is being circulated with a follow-up meeting possible, an official briefed on the talks said on Monday.

The negotiators departed on Sunday, though not because of difficulties in the negotiations, the official said, without providing further details on the draft proposal.

Iran's foreign ministry spokesperson said the basis of the talks is a seven-step plan Iran drew up in September to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and end the US naval blockade on Iran, with Tehran now suggesting that proposal could be implemented on a faster timeline under a deal.

The spokesperson, Esmaeil Baghaei, said deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi had been in Doha to facilitate the exchange of messages with Washington via Qatari intermediaries.

"Our demands have been articulated very clearly and transparently. These demands are reasonable and logical: no final agreement can be initiated, nor can the Strait of Hormuz be reopened or secured, unless the US naval blockade is brought to an end, Iran's demands are respected, and Iran’s legitimate requirements are addressed,” Baghaei said.

Reporting by AFP and Reuters

item.title: [World news | The Guardian] Burnham declines to say net migration still too high as Mahmood prepares to unveil tougher settlement rules – UK politics live
item.description:
Home secretary to make some migrants wait 10 years or more for right to settle in UK

Chris Philp, the shadow home secretary, is already ridiculing the indefinite leave to remain (ILR) announcement coming this afternoon. In a post on social media, he claimed that she was surrendering to “the open-borders Labour left”.

Later today the government will announce their u-turn on ILR, or Indefinite Leave to Remain.

It’s clear Shabana Mahmood has been forced to surrender to Angela Rayner and the open-borders Labour left. She will now allow hundreds of thousands of low-wage and no-wage migrants to stay in the UK forever and claim benefits.

The Labour Party is at war with itself over Indefinite Leave to Remain (ILR), with Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood losing a fight to the far left of her own party. Tomorrow, she’s expected to cave on plans to even tinker with the ILR numbers. Angela Rayner emerges victorious, with her defence of the Tory-era policies hinging on “fair play” towards foreign nationals.

But what about fair play towards the British public? Doesn’t that count for anything anymore? Villages, towns, suburbs, and cities have to deal with the weight and strain of all this. Not only are ordinary Brits never consulted, but this current cabinet doesn’t even have an electoral mandate. It is rightly infuriating to most people who increasingly want net negative migration into Britain.
